description: Every year, 20 million people receive a life-altering cancer diagnosis, a staggering reality that became deeply personal for oncology researcher Rodrigo Toledo when his own father was diagnosed. Drawing from his pioneering work with "liquid biopsies" at the Vall d’Hebron Institute of Oncology, Rodrigo explains how simple blood tests are revolutionizing the way we track and treat tumors. However, he emphasizes that defeating cancer cannot be left to scientists alone and challenges everyone to take an active role in their health. To help you shift the odds in your favor, Rodrigo shares three science-backed habits. Whether you are a survivor or looking to protect your future health, this powerful talk leaves you with one vital question: what are you going to do about it? Dr. Rodrigo Toledo holds a PhD in Human Genetics and leads the Biomarker and Clonal Dynamics Group at the Vall d’Hebron Institute of Oncology (VHIO) in Barcelona. author: TEDx Talks
description:
This isn’t a talk about failure. It’s about what happens after success; when praise masks damage, exhaustion is mistaken for drive, and the most dangerous lie becomes “I’m fine.” Through raw, deeply personal stories spanning five countries and four decades, Sean Finter reveals how the beliefs installed early in life quietly hijack our health, relationships, and sense of self. This talk dismantles the myth that more discipline, more grit, or more success will fix what’s actually breaking underneath.

If you’re successful, composed, and pretending not to notice the check-engine light, this talk isn’t a coincidence. You’ll leave with a choice most people only get after something breaks. Sean Finter has held nearly every role in the bar and restaurant business, starting as a dishwasher in a small town in Canada, owning and operating venues in Sydney, and eventually building one of the industry's largest global consultancies in the U.S.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
“Et si je vous disais que nous sommes toutes et tous atteint d'une forme de cécité ? Pas une perte de vue physique, mais une incapacité psychologique à percevoir ce qui nous entoure le plus : les plantes.”

Dans cette intervention captivante, Marie Forêt, ingénieure agronome spécialisée en écologie, nous révèle le phénomène de la "cécité végétale". Elle nous explique pourquoi notre cerveau ignore instinctivement les végétaux pour se concentrer sur le mouvement, et comment ce manque d'attention met aujourd'hui notre avenir en péril.

Dans cette vidéo, vous découvrez :
- Le test de la vache : Pourquoi notre regard ignore le décor naturel au profit de l'animal.
- Une dépendance vitale : Des médicaments (aspirine, taxol) à nos vêtements et notre alimentation, les plantes assurent notre survie.
- Les dangers de l'indifférence : Comment notre "aveuglement" facilite la destruction des habitats et la propagation d'espèces invasives comme la Renouée du Japon.
- Réapprendre à voir : L'intervena
title: Pourquoi voyez-vous la vache, mais pas la prairie ! | Marie FORÊT | TEDxClermont

description:
In this deeply personal and thought-provoking talk, Susan Houston explores the hidden force that shapes our decisions long before we realize it: Second Hand Doubt — the judgments, biases, and expectations we absorb from others and mistake for our own voice.
Over time, these inherited narratives influence the risks we take, the relationships we stay in, and the dreams we quietly abandon. They teach us to apologize too quickly, stay silent to stay safe, and question our worth before we ever step forward.
Through powerful storytelling and practical insight, Susan challenges audiences to recognize the doubt they didn’t choose, interrupt its influence, and reclaim authorship of their lives.
Because the most dangerous limitations are rarely the ones spoken out loud — they’re the ones we’ve been carrying for years.

Having lived across different countries and cultures — including extended periods in Latin America and Europe — Noel developed a strong interest in how young people make life-defining decisions in increasingly global environments.
Through his work with students and families, he has seen how difficult it can be to choose a path when expectations, social pressure, and uncertainty collide.
In his talk, Noel reflects on how most of the important decisions in life are made with incomplete information, and why learning to navigate uncertainty may be one of the most valuable skills we rarely teach. title: Who are We Becoming when We Stop Choosing for Ourselves? | Noel Cortes | TEDxUWCMaastricht

description:
. Anya is a 17-year-old residential student at UWC Maastricht. Born and raised in Mexico City, she’s passionate about impacting those around her and helping find growth in the potential she sees around her, getting involved in refugee initiatives in both Mexico and the Netherlands and taking part in community events such as the International Peace Conference. She loves swimming, cooking for the people she cares about and has a particular enjoyment for deep existentialist conversations over good food. She’s always questioning how we think about everyday things and looking for new ways to understand the world.
In her TEDx talk, Anya challenges the misconceptions we have about balance and presents a new way to approach it through her own experiences and observations. author: TEDx Talks
description:
. Lluís was born in Barcelona and is growing up in the Netherlands. Moving between cultures has taught him one thing pretty quickly - that knowing how to introduce yourself isnt the same as knowing how to connect with others.
At 16, he has been in debates, conferences, sponsor events, and school leadership roles where “networking” is always mentioned as something you’re supposed to master. But most of the time it just ends up feeling awkward. Either people are trying too hard to impress, or they’re too quiet to say anything at all.
Through his Ted talk “Everyone is networking. Almost no one is connecting.” he wants to explore why conversations feel transactional, why young people often underestimate their value in a room, and what changes when you focus less on getting something and more on building something real. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

Much has been written about betrayal in the worlds of espionage and conflict. But what if the most dangerous betrayal of all happens every day -  in the small, repeated decisions that pull us away from who we know we are meant to be?

. Sheila (or Xinyu—her Chinese name) was born in Shanghai, China. Despite growing up in a gigantic city, she prefers nature: hiking, mountaineering, and rock climbing. Physical adventures bring her mental peace.

description: . Berfu Ege Sobe is an impact maker at the intersection of finance, law, and sustainable development. Working with SNV, one of the world’s leading international development organisations, she designs large-scale programmes and builds the funding strategies that bring them to life, mobilising multi-million euro resources and forging the partnerships that make real change possible. Berfu believes that sustainable development is a goal that everyone should know about. Because with the right partnerships, the right funding, and the right focus, we can achieve it.
